messages:
emily: Drafting a small docs PR for a 'signed-proxy' pattern to support air-gapped/private installs. Idea: installer speaks to a short-lived signing proxy in a DMZ which forwards PKCS#11 calls to the HSM. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/docs/pull/4477

ryan: Can we add a compact network diagram and explicit port list? Proposal: installer -> proxy (8443), proxy -> hsm (5696). Also include a firewall rule snippet and a curl healthcheck.

tara: Security note: emphasise the threat model: keys never leave HSM. Proxy only forwards sign requests and should never write key material to disk. Recommend mTLS + short tokens and audit headers (x-request-id, x-operator).

emily: Will add a tiny preflight script for installers:
```
# from installer host
nc -zv proxy.example.com 8443 || echo "proxy unreachable"
curl --cacert proxy-ca.pem https://proxy.example.com:8443/v1/health
```

ryan: Please include a Python example for calling the proxy (requests + mTLS) and a note to encrypt tokens in the airgap bundle rather than embedding them raw.

tara: Also document return semantics when HSM is unreachable: 503 with {"error":"hsm-unavailable","retry_after":30}. Helps automated installers handle backoff.

emily: Good call. I'll mark all snippets "example only" and add a troubleshooting note about CA bundle size limits if any.

ops-bot: PR created: https://git.internal/redwood/docs/pull/4477  reviewers: @ryan @tara

emily: Thanks — aiming to push the draft tonight; will wait for security + network quick reviews before merging.
